blocs.texte: L'impératif sert à donner des ordres, des instructions ou des conseils. Il s'utilise beaucoup en classe pour les consignes.
Forme affirmative : on utilise la base verbale sans sujet. Exemple : Open your book. Forme négative : Don't + base verbale. Exemple : Don't talk during the test.

lignes: Take out a sheet of paper.
Ne parle pas pendant le contrôle.

blocs.texte: Pendant une pause en classe, le professeur propose le jeu 'Teacher Says' (comme 'Jacques a dit'). Il donne des ordres à l'impératif, et les élèves ne doivent les exécuter que si l'ordre commence par 'Teacher says'. Exemple : 'Teacher says: Stand up!' (les élèves se lèvent) — 'Sit down!' (sans 'Teacher says', les élèves ne doivent pas bouger) — 'Teacher says: Touch your nose!' (les élèves touchent leur nez). Ce jeu permet de pratiquer l'impératif de façon ludique.

blocs.enonce: Transforme ces phrases en ordres à l'impératif (affirmatif ou négatif selon le sens) : 1) You should open the window. 2) You must not run in the corridor. 3) You have to finish your homework. 4) You should not eat in class. 5) You need to be on time.
blocs.solution: 1) Open the window. 2) Don't run in the corridor. 3) Finish your homework. 4) Don't eat in class. 5) Be on time.

blocs.texte: Le discours rapporté (reported speech) permet de rapporter les paroles de quelqu'un sans les citer mot à mot.

blocs.titre: Structure du discours rapporté (ordres et requêtes)
blocs.texte: Affirmatif : sujet + verbe introducteur (tell / ask / order / command...) + complément (la personne) + TO + base verbale. Exemple : 'Close the door,' she said to him. → She told him to close the door. Négatif : sujet + verbe introducteur + complément + NOT TO + base verbale. Exemple : 'Don't touch that,' he said to her. → He told her not to touch that. Remarque : on n'utilise pas 'that', et le verbe passe à l'infinitif avec 'to'.

lignes: The officer ordered the soldiers to march.
The general commanded the troops to retreat.
The manager requested the staff to arrive early.
The doctor advised him to rest.

blocs.texte: 1) Direct : 'Tidy your room,' Nancy said to her sister. → Rapporté : Nancy told her sister to tidy her room. 2) Direct : 'Don't touch my phone,' Nancy said to her sister. → Rapporté : Nancy told her sister not to touch her phone. 3) Direct : 'Please help me with the dishes,' Nancy said to her sister. → Rapporté : Nancy asked her sister to help her with the dishes. 4) Direct : 'Don't be late for dinner,' Nancy said to her sister. → Rapporté : Nancy told her sister not to be late for dinner.

blocs.enonce: Rapporte les phrases suivantes au discours rapporté : 1) 'Open your books,' the teacher said to the students. 2) 'Don't run in the classroom,' the teacher said to the pupils. 3) 'Please sit down,' she said to him. 4) 'Don't forget your homework,' he said to them. 5) 'Clean the board,' the teacher said to the monitor.
blocs.solution: 1) The teacher told the students to open their books. 2) The teacher told the pupils not to run in the classroom. 3) She asked him to sit down. 4) He told them not to forget their homework. 5) The teacher told the monitor to clean the board.

blocs.texte: On peut aussi rapporter des citations célèbres formulées à l'impératif, en appliquant la même règle que pour les ordres et requêtes : sujet + verbe introducteur + to/not to + base verbale.

1) Citation de Maya Angelou (pour encourager) : 'Do the best you can until you know better. Then when you know better, do better.' → Rapportée : Maya Angelou told people to do the best they could until they knew better, and to do better when they knew better. 2) Citation d'Albert Einstein (pour inspirer) : 'Try not to become a man of success, but rather try to become a man of value.' → Rapportée : Einstein told people to try not to become a man of success, but rather to try to become a man of value. 3) Citation populaire (pour donner de l'espoir) : 'Don't give up. Look for the rainbow after the cloud, and always keep hope alive.' → Rapportée : She told them not to give up, to look for the rainbow after the cloud, and to always keep hope alive.

blocs.titre: Rapporter plusieurs ordres dans une même phrase
blocs.texte: Quand une citation contient plusieurs ordres reliés par 'and' ou 'then', on garde 'and' ou 'and then', et on répète 'to' (ou 'not to' si négatif) devant chaque verbe. Exemple : Direct : 'Be kind and help others.' → Rapporté : She told us to be kind and to help others.

blocs.enonce: Rapporte ces 4 citations célèbres formulées à l'impératif (attention aux verbes multiples) : 1) 'Believe in yourself and never give up.' 2) 'Dream big and work hard.' 3) 'Always be yourself and don't be afraid to fail.' 4) 'Follow your passion and stay strong.'
blocs.solution: 1) He told them to believe in themselves and never to give up. 2) She told them to dream big and to work hard. 3) He told them to always be themselves and not to be afraid to fail. 4) She told them to follow their passion and to stay strong.
